tool.provenance: The official release checksum table publishes this SHA-1. The cached jar matches it. SHA-256 was computed over those same bytes and is enforced before execution. Java and the jar are never committed.
tool.mode: Breadth-first complete reachable-state exploration. No simulation, depth cutoff, fairness or temporal liveness property. Terminal deadlocks are permitted.

bounds.retryOrder: The same request restarts. When a already exists, either lexical order of a and b is allowed. This overapproximates symbolic hash ordering after importOrder reads a valid existing prefix.
bounds.observer: One captured subset of currently visible hashes, arbitrary per-record read order, separate record and evidence reads, then reference validation.
bounds.orphanAbstraction: Keep one existence bit per writer. A crashed pending directory's fresh name and file stage cannot affect any later modeled action. All partial/completion stages remain explicit before the crash.

assumptions: Content hashes are collision-free and file completion writes exactly the requested symbolic bytes.
Every pending directory name is fresh, ordinary and disjoint from canonical hash names.
Directory rename within the same filesystem is atomic. A duplicate nonempty canonical destination is preserved and the writer reads it back.
No external deletion, mutation, symlink substitution or power loss occurs.
The modeled import begins after complete preparation and reference validation over a valid existing store.
Successful filesystem operations and duplicate-destination collisions are modeled. Unexpected I/O errors and cleanup failures are excluded.
Pure validation and metadata guards around immutable file reads are silent steps. Recursive cleanup only removes an unobservable pending directory.
TLC's fixed fingerprint implementation is trusted subject to its logged collision estimate. A pass is bounded model evidence, not a universal proof.

properties.promise: Every visible canonical directory contains both complete matching files.
properties.harm: A partial canonical record can corrupt later responsibility reviews.

properties.promise: For the configured retainImport caller, visible b always has visible dependency a.
properties.scope: publishRecord alone has no dependency-order promise.

properties.promise: Every successful record/evidence readback matches a requested hash and complete canonical bytes.
Every returned publication remains visible through later interleavings and retries.
A completed plan returns exactly its requested hashes, including after a retry.
properties.scope: Conditional safety only. No eventual retry or completion guarantee.

properties.promise: An accepted reader manifest contains its dependencies and complete matching files.
properties.scope: Reference-incomplete captured lists may be refused. No atomic snapshot promise.

mapping.boundary: Collision-free symbolic contents abstract canonical hashing and expected file digests.
Directory creation, each write's partial/completed bytes, atomic rename, separate readbacks and pending-only cleanup remain separate.
Metadata guards are silent under ordinary immutable-file assumptions. Each file read and final reference validation remain separate.
Initial validated two-record plan is dependency-first. A new call may use either order if the dependency already exists. Arbitrary direct publishers are excluded from dependency promises.
A process can stop between mapped operations. A fresh same-input call leaves old pending names ignored and uses a new unique pending directory.

mutations.sourceChange: Copied publishRecord uses destination as pending.
mutations.requiredWitness: The requested canonical hash directory exists with neither expected file before the child is killed.
A complete successor exists and its actual supersedes.hash names an absent predecessor directory.

excluded: Arbitrary-size bundles, all record-type reference validation and full parser input domains.
Unbounded retries, fairness, liveness, filesystem flushes and power-loss durability.
Arbitrary I/O errors, cleanup failures and hostile external filesystem mutation.
A globally atomic readStore or responsibility review snapshot.
Native dispatch, at-most-once execution, provider authentication or authority, accounts, schedules, delivery, merge and deployment.

Cloud lineage and direct cloud caller dependency graph, cooperative admission/retries/checkpoints, turn claim ownership/recovery, telemetry, pending escalation and cloud archive/restore semantics. These have separate finite and CLI controls.
Atomic exclusion of concurrent cloud claim acquisition during backup; unresolved-claim refusal is a preflight check.

Derived improvement report hard-link publication, cooperative guard/token release, source-age read projection and supplied token accounting. Their unit and actual CLI controls are separate from canonical journal TLC properties.
